I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It has no lodash imports, and the exported signatures are the same as in `src/module.ts`.

- **`applyPatch`** now uses `merge` from `es-toolkit`. A quick check showed it gives the same result as the compat `merge` on a sample patch: arrays merged by index, a null base replaced by an object, and nested objects merged. I couldn't compare against lodash directly because it isn't installed.
- **`toTitle`** uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main `startCase` doesn't match lodash. It gives `ID` → `Id` and `AB1C` → `Ab 1 C`, where lodash keeps `ID` and gives `AB 1 C`. Your input range includes consecutive capitals, so I used the compat version.
- **`preview`** uses `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`, because es-toolkit's main entry has no `truncate`.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` printed 2364 bytes min+gzip and 97 bytes of own code. Using compat for `merge` as well came to 4044 bytes, so I kept the main `merge`.

I couldn't get a size for the original lodash version, because `npm run size` fails on `src/module.ts`. I also couldn't type-check the new file on its own. `tsc` runs on `src/module.ts` and reports it can't find the lodash modules, since lodash isn't installed. I didn't confirm that `out/module.ts` is part of the project's type-check, and I didn't run `tsc` on it separately.
